## Historical audit — S0305

**Source for all citations:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/development/commons_192968130/1/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines and supplied character ranges.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Goal: H request, line 1 [0,11553) | Reconstruct a single indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching camera and appearance. The student’s kitchen inventory is an interpretation of the image, not independent evidence of its contents. |
| Initial build: H response and execution, lines 3 [0,10464), 4 [0,10179) | Code creates multiple assets: architecture, slatted wall, door with handle, cabinetry, hob, inset and hood. Parts are grouped through `include` and positioned by coordinates; physical connection and reference correctness are not verified. It specifies colors, a conditional procedural stone material, burner rings, camera and lights. No articulated pose is at issue in the described static scene; placement remains unverified. |
| First validation and revision: lines 6 [0,1659), 8 [0,1645), 11 [0,42478), 13–14 [0,8024), [0,7742) | Build and render completed; the render was supplied to H. H reported a small, centered door and back wall, excess blank wall and floor. It then moved the camera closer, shifted the hob, darkened cabinetry and reduced lighting. The second program omits the first program’s procedural countertop shader. These are H’s visual judgments, not independent verification. |
| Second revision: H response and execute, lines 23–24 [0,9849), [0,9565) | H reported low wall/door framing, cabinetry and counter too far right, an out-of-frame hob, missing veining and light cabinetry. It changed camera aim, widened cabinetry and counter, moved the hob, extended slats, darkened lighting and added a dimension-selected procedural stone shader. Execution is separately recorded. |
| Outcome: lines 16, 18–20, 26, 28–30 [0,1654), [0,1647), [0,20781), [0,59), [0,1656), [0,1646), [0,20659), [0,59) | Steps 2 and 3 built and rendered successfully; step 3 was selected. This is **technical execution success**, not formal visual or geometric success. No final image inspection or `DONE` is visible. Whether the shader matched its intended mesh, parts align, or final framing and lighting improved is unknown. No timeout or algorithm failure is recorded. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student receipt is visible. The system instructions were actually supplied to H, and the subsequent inventory, renders and revisions are consistent with their workflow; that does not establish adoption of any unseen teacher advice. H autonomously revised after runner-provided images; its sessions report no tool calls, with backend request counts unknown (lines 2 [0,3782), 12 [0,4305), 22 [0,4833)).

**Transferable lesson:** successful rendering and named hierarchy establish executable output, not image completeness or connected geometry. Comparing renders can motivate camera and local-object hypotheses, but simultaneous changes make causality uncertain. **Task-specific hypothesis:** moving the camera and hob may address H’s reported framing issues; the unseen final image cannot confirm it. The reference and renders themselves are not supplied as viewable pixels in this audit, so materials, multiple-object coverage, occlusions and final similarity remain unresolved.
